00da8541     Computes the result of passing an input vector X into a fully
00da8583     connected layer with 2D weight matrix W and 1D bias vector b. That is,
00da85ce     the layer computes Y = X * W^T + b, where X has size (M x K),
00da8610     W has size (N x K), b has size (N), and Y has size (M x N),
00da8650     where M is often the batch size.
00da8677     NOTE: X does not need to explicitly be a 2D vector; rather, it will be
00da86c2     coerced into one. For an arbitrary n-dimensional tensor
00da86fe     X \in [a_0, a_1, ...,a_{k-1}, a_k, ..., a_{n-1}] where a_i \in N+ and k is
00da874d     the axis provided, then X will be coerced into a 2-dimensional tensor with
00da879c     dimensions [a_0 * ... * a_{k-1}, a_k * ... * a_{n-1}]. For the default
00da87e7     case where axis=1, this means the X tensor will be coerced into a 2D tensor
00da8837     of dimensions [a_0, a_1 * ... * a_{n-1}], where a_0 is often the batch size.
00da8888     In this situation, we must have a_0 = M and a_1 * ... * a_{n-1} = K.
00da88d1     Lastly, even though b is a 1D vector of size N, it is copied/resized to
00da891d     be size (M x N) implicitly and added to each vector in the batch.
00da8963     Each of these dimensions must be matched correctly, or else the operator
00da89b0     will throw errors.

00da8a58 Applies 8-bit row-wise quantization by determining the range
00da8a95       (maximum - minimum) and offset (minimum value) of each row in the input
00da8ae3       matrix, and then scaling each element to an 8-bit number between 0 and
00da8b30       255. To later de-quantize values, the scale (range / 255) and offset
00da8b7b       (bias) are stored alongside the data. More precisely, the first 4 bytes
00da8bc9       of each row in the output matrix are a 32-bit float storing the scale,

00da8c61       bytes in the row encode single quantized values.

00da8d74       followed by the bias as a 32-bit float in the next 4 bytes, followed by
00da8dc2       the quantized values in the remaining bytes of the row. The output is a
00da8e10       matrix containing only the values, but de-quantized. De-quantization is

00da9b71 Hierarchical softmax is an operator which approximates the softmax operator
00da9bbd while giving significant training speed gains and reasonably comparable
00da9c05 performance. In this operator, instead of calculating the probabilities of all
00da9c54 the classes, we calculate the probability of each step in the path from root to
00da9ca4 the target word in the hierarchy.
00da9cc7 The operator takes a 2-D tensor (Tensor<float>) containing a batch of layers, a
00da9d17 set of parameters represented by the weight matrix and bias terms, and a 1-D
00da9d64 tensor (Tensor<int>) holding labels, or the indices of the target class. The
00da9db1 hierarchy has to be specified as an argument to the operator.
00da9df0 The operator returns a 1-D tensor holding the computed log probability of the
00da9e3e target class and a 2-D tensor of intermediate outputs (from the weight matrix
00da9e8c and softmax from each step in the path from root to target class) which will be
00da9edc used by the gradient operator to compute gradients for all samples in the batch.

00dac338 This operator applies 8Bit row-wise quantization to
00dac36c     input tensor and returns quantized tensor. Row wise quantization of
00dac3b4     input tensor is the following process. We take tensor of size
00dac3f6     (m_1, m_2,...,m_n), n >= 2, reshape it into matrix of size
00dac435     (m_1, m_2 x... x m_n) and apply row-wise quantization. After this,
00dac47c     we compute scale_i= (min_i - max_i) / 255 and  bias_i = min_i for
00dac4c2     i-th row r_i of reshaped matrix, where min_i and max_i --  minimum
00dac509     and maximum elements of i-th row, and quantize each element r_{ij} as
00dac553     0 <= round(r_ij - bias_i) / scale_i) < 256. Instead of input tensor
00dac59b     we obtain uint8 tensor and auxiliary information as scale and bias to
00dac5e5     restore input tensor (with losses).
00dac610 Given uint8 tensor, quantized using 8bit row-wise
00dac642     quantization, and auxiliary scales and biases, this operator
00dac683     restores float tensor in the following way. We take input 8bits tensor
00dac6ce     of size  (m_1, m_2, ..., m_n), n >= 2, reshape it  into matrix of size
00dac719     (m_1, m_2 x... x m_n). We compute element r_{ij} of output matrix as
00dac762     r_{ij} * s_i + b_i and after this we reshape this output matrix into
00dac7ab     output tensor of size (m_1, m_2, ..., m_n).

00dae7e1 MergeIdLists: Merge multiple ID_LISTs into a single ID_LIST.
00dae81f An ID_LIST is a list of IDs (may be ints, often longs) that represents a single
00dae86f feature. As described in https://caffe2.ai/docs/sparse-operations.html, a batch
00dae8bf of ID_LIST examples is represented as a pair of lengths and values where the
00dae90c `lengths` (int32) segment the `values` or ids (int32/int64) into examples.
00dae958 Given multiple inputs of the form lengths_0, values_0, lengths_1, values_1, ...
00dae9a8 which correspond to lengths and values of ID_LISTs of different features, this
00dae9f7 operator produces a merged ID_LIST that combines the ID_LIST features. The
00daea42 final merged output is described by a lengths and values vector.
00daea84 WARNING: The merge makes no guarantee about the relative order of ID_LISTs
00daeacf within a batch. This can be an issue if ID_LIST are order sensitive.

00db6a72 the axis provided, then X will be coerced into a 2-dimensional tensor with
00db6abd dimensions [a_0 * ... * a_{k-1}, a_k * ... * a_{n-1}]. For the default
00db6b04 case where axis=1, this means the X tensor will be coerced into a 2D tensor

00dba120 /home/nshulga/git/caffe2/caffe2/operators/tt_linear_op.cc
00dba161 The TT-layer serves as a low-rank decomposition of a fully connected layer. The
00dba1b1 inputs are the same as to a fully connected layer, but the number of parameters
00dba201 are greatly reduced and forward computation time can be drastically reduced
00dba24d especially for layers with large weight matrices. The multiplication is computed
00dba29e as a product of the input vector with each of the cores that make up the TT
00dba2ea layer. Given the input sizes (inp_sizes), output sizes(out_sizes), and the ranks
00dba33b of each of the cores (tt_ranks), the ith core will have size:
00dba37a     inp_sizes[i] * tt_ranks[i] * tt_ranks[i + 1] * out_sizes[i].
00dba3bc The complexity of the computation is dictated by the sizes of inp_sizes,
00dba405 out_sizes, and tt_ranks, where there is the trade off between accuracy of the
00dba453 low-rank decomposition and the speed of the computation.

00dbe360 /home/nshulga/git/caffe2/caffe2/sgd/adam_op.cc
00dbe392 Computes the Adam update (https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6980) for an
00dbe3d4 input gradient and momentum parameters. Concretely, given inputs
00dbe415 (param, m1, m2, grad, lr, iters),
00dbe438     t = iters + 1
00dbe44a     corrected_local_rate = lr * sqrt(1 - power(beta2, t)) /
00dbe486       (1 - power(beta1, t))
00dbe4a2     m1_o = (beta1 * m1) + (1 - beta1) * grad
00dbe4cf     m2_o = (beta2 * m2) + (1 - beta2) * np.square(grad)
00dbe507     grad_o = corrected_local_rate * m1_o / \
00dbe534         (sqrt(m2_o) + epsilon)
00dbe553     param_o = param + grad_o

00dbebd9 Learning rate is a decreasing function of time. With low learning rates the
00dbec25 improvements will be linear. With high learning rates they will start to look
00dbec73 more exponential. Learning rate is controlled by the following arguments:
00dbecbe #### Required
00dbeccd * `iterations`
00dbecdc * `base_lr`: base learning rate
00dbecfc * `policy`: this controls how the learning rate is applied, options are:
00dbed45   * `fixed`
00dbed51   * `step`: uses `stepsize`, `gamma`
00dbed76   * `exp`: uses `gamma`
00dbed8e   * `inv`: uses `gamma`, `power`
00dbedaf   * `linearWarmup`: uses `start_multiplier`, `num_iter`
00dbede7   * `constantWarmup`: uses `multiplier`, `num_iter`
00dbee1b   * `alter`: uses  `active_first`, `active_period`, `inactive_period`
00dbee61   * `hill`: uses those in both `linearWarmup` and `inv`, plus `end_multiplier`
00dbeeb2 ### Optional:

00dbf148 MomentumSGD
00dbf158 /home/nshulga/git/caffe2/caffe2/sgd/momentum_sgd_op.cc
00dbf192 Computes a momentum SGD update for an input gradient and momentum
00dbf1d4 parameters. Concretely, given inputs (grad, m, lr) and parameters
00dbf216 (momentum, nesterov), computes:
00dbf237     if not nesterov:
00dbf24c         adjusted_gradient = lr * grad + momentum * m
00dbf281         return (adjusted_gradient, adjusted_gradient)
00dbf2b7     else:
00dbf2c1         m_new = momentum * m + lr * grad
00dbf2ea         return ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m, m_new)
00dbf329 Output is (grad, momentum)
00dbf345 Note the difference to MomemtumSGDUpdate, which actually performs the
00dbf38b parameter update (and is thus faster).
00dbf3b8 MomentumSGDUpdate
00dbf3d2 Performs a momentum SGD update for an input gradient and momentum
00dbf414 parameters. Concretely, given inputs (grad, m, lr, param) and arguments
00dbf45c (momentum, nesterov), computes:
00dbf47d     if not nesterov:
00dbf492         adjusted_gradient = lr * grad + momentum * m
00dbf4c7         param = param - adjusted_gradient
00dbf4f1         return (adjusted_gradient, adjusted_gradient, param)
00dbf52e     else:
00dbf538         m_new = momentum * m + lr * grad
00dbf561         param = param - ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m),
00dbf5a2         return ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m, m_new, param)
00dbf5e8 Output is (grad, momentum, parameter).
00dbf610 Note the difference to MomentumSGD, which returns a new gradient
00dbf651 but does not perform the parameter update.
00dbf680 SparseMomentumSGDUpdate

00dbf6e5 GradientSlice and indices into the full param and momentum tables. Both param
00dbf733 and momentum should be in-place (corresponding inputs and outputs should be the
00dbf783 same blobs).
00dbf798 RmsProp

00dbf7da Computes the RMSProp update
00dbf7f6 (http://www.cs.toronto.edu/~tijmen/csc321/slides/lecture_slides_lec6.pdf).
00dbf841 Concretely, given inputs (grad, mean_squares, mom, lr), computes:
00dbf884     mean_squares_o = mean_squares + (1 - decay) * (square(grad) - mean_squares)
00dbf8d4     mom_o = momentum * mom + lr * grad / sqrt(epsilon + mean_squares_o)
00dbf91c     grad_o = mom_o
00dbf930 returns (grad_o, mean_squares_o, mom_o).
